title: The Bag of Winds
text:
In Homer's Odyssey, on his long voyage home from Troy, Odysseus came with his twelve ships to the floating island of Aeolus, keeper of the winds. Aeolus treated them kindly for a month, and when they left, he gave Odysseus a remarkable gift: a bag of oxhide, tied shut with a silver cord, in which he had shut up all the stormy winds. Only the gentle West Wind was left free, to blow the ships straight home.

For nine days and nights they sailed, and Odysseus himself held the sail's rope the whole time, trusting it to no one. On the tenth day they came so close to Ithaca that they could see men tending fires on the shore. Then, worn out at last, Odysseus fell asleep.

His crew began to talk. Everywhere their captain went, people gave him treasure, and now this bag. It must be full of gold and silver, and he was keeping it for himself while they came home with nothing. They untied the bag to see.

The winds burst out all at once. A storm tore the ships away from Ithaca and drove them all the way back to Aeolus's island. When Odysseus begged for help again, Aeolus drove him away, saying that a man so hated by the gods would get no more help from him.
lesson: Suspicion inside a team can destroy a success that is almost won. Leaders who keep their crew in the dark invite rumors, and crews that act on rumors can lose everything.
